actions.body: Process continuity in rational agents is closely tied to the stability of world models and long-term objective optimization. Without reliable process preservation, agents face significant coordination and optimization hurdles across multi-objective environments. Empirical findings from multi-objective reinforcement learning and curiosity-driven frameworks illustrate that while agents can adapt to changing conditions, maintaining consistent optimization trajectories requires clear structural bounds. Summary: This research explores why rational agents benefit from preserving their ongoing processes over time, showing that continuous world models and stable optimization frameworks are essential for long-term task success.
